definitions.gloss: sure enough; as expected; just as one thought
definitions.explanation: Used when something happens exactly as one predicted or worried it would, often with slightly negative expectations.

examples.japanese: {案|あん}の{定|じょう}、{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れた。
examples.english: Sure enough, I missed the train.

examples.japanese: {案|あん}の{定|じょう}、{彼|かれ}は{約束|やくそく}を{忘|わす}れていた。
examples.english: As expected, he had forgotten the promise.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうだと{思|おも}ったら、{案|あん}の{定|じょう}{降|ふ}ってきた。
examples.english: I thought it looked like rain, and sure enough, it started raining.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{案|あん} (plan, expectation) + の (possessive) + {定|じょう} (fixed, determined)
Literally: "as the expectation was fixed" → "just as expected"

USAGE NOTES:
Typically used when a negative or undesirable outcome that was anticipated actually occurs. Less commonly used for positive surprises.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・やはり/やっぱり - as expected (more neutral, can be positive or negative)
・{思|おも}った{通|とお}り - just as I thought
・{予想|よそう}{通|どお}り - as predicted
・{果|は}たして - as expected, sure enough (more literary)

CONTRAST:
・{意外|いがい}にも - unexpectedly
・{思|おも}いのほか - more than expected
